Complete Empirical Research Plan

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Primary method: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (FRD) combined with a local Wald (2-stage) estimator.  
Rationale  
• The institutional rule (investment-grade vs. speculative-grade) is determined by a sharp numerical cut-off in the underlying rating score.  
• Crossing this cut-off causes a large, discontinuous jump in credit spreads that is otherwise smooth in the rating score.  
• We can therefore use the rating-score distance from the cut-off as the running variable. The discontinuous change in spreads provides an exogenous first-stage that instruments for the endogenous credit spread when estimating its causal impact on prices and trading behavior.

-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Running variable: rating_score ≡ an integer that rises as credit quality worsens (AAA=1, AA+=2, …, CCC–=21).  
Cut-off: score* = 10.5, which lies between BBB– (score 10) and BB+ (score 11), the regulatory boundary between investment-grade and high-yield.  

Treatment indicator Zi  
Zi = 1 if rating_scorei ≥ 11 (speculative grade)  
Zi = 0 if rating_scorei ≤ 10 (investment grade)  

Because not every observation exactly at score* moves mechanically into a different spread, the design is fuzzy.  

• “Treated” observations: bonds with rating_score right above the cut-off (11,12,…) within a chosen bandwidth h.  
• “Control” observations: bonds with rating_score right below the cut-off (10,9,…) within the same bandwidth.  

Event timing: we focus on the first rating announcement in each calendar year. Outcomes (price, trading volume) are measured the next trading day to avoid micro-structure noise, but we will replicate results at horizons of 5, 20, and 60 trading days.

-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes. Bond prices and trading volumes would evolve smoothly in rating_score in the absence of the discrete regulatory reclassification.  
Plausibility: rating agencies map detailed scorecards into letter grades mechanically; no additional simultaneous shocks occur exactly at 10.5.

A2. No precise manipulation of the rating score around the cut-off.  
Plausibility: issuers cannot predict exactly which committee members will decide the score; historical audits show “rating creep” occurs over months, not single notches.

A3. First-stage relevance. Crossing the cut-off must generate a statistically significant jump in credit spreads.  
Plausibility: The IG/HY boundary is well known to create 100–200 bp jumps in OAS spreads.

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA). One bond’s rating change does not directly alter the outcome of another bond within the estimation window.  
Plausibility: realistic at the bond level; we will cluster standard errors at the issuer level.

-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
-------------------------------------------------
T1. Manipulation of the running variable (rating shopping).  
Check & Fix: Run the McCrary (2008) density test (rddensity). If a discontinuity in the density is detected, widen the bandwidth or use a donut RD excluding ±0.5 notches.

T2. Differential information releases at the cut-off (e.g., analysts change outlooks simultaneously).  
Check & Fix: Balance tests for predetermined covariates (issue size, maturity, sector). We will also estimate RD in pre-rating periods as placebo tests.

T3. Spillovers/liquidity externalities (downgrade of one bond affects all HY bonds).  
Check & Fix: Include HY market-wide controls (HY ETF returns, VIX) in the second stage and cluster by date in addition to issuer.

-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
#############################
# 0. Packages
#############################
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast FELM / IV
library(rdrobust)    # RD estimation
library(rddensity)   # McCrary test
set.seed(123)

#############################
# 1. Load & clean data
#############################
dat <- fread("bond_panel_2000_2010.csv")

# Map ratings to numeric score
rating_map <- data.table(letter = c("AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-",
                                    "BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-",
                                    "B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-","CC","C"),
                         score  = 1:21)
dat <- merge(dat, rating_map, by = "letter")
dat[, running := score - 10.5]        # center at the cut-off
dat[, treat  := as.integer(running >= 0)]

#############################
# 2. Bandwidth selection
#############################
bw <- rdbwselect(y = dat$credit_spread, x = dat$running)$bws[1]  # Imbens–Kalyanaraman

dat_rdd <- dat[abs(running) <= bw]        # keep local window

#############################
# 3. First-stage: jump in spreads
#############################
fs <- rdrobust(y = dat_rdd$credit_spread,
               x = dat_rdd$running, c = 0,
               p = 1, h = bw, fuzzy = dat_rdd$treat)

print(fs)

#############################
# 4. Second stage (local Wald)
#############################
# rdrobust can report the Wald estimate directly when fuzzy != NULL
w_out <- rdrobust(y = dat_rdd$bond_price,   # outcome of interest
                  x = dat_rdd$running,
                  fuzzy = dat_rdd$treat,
                  p = 1, h = bw)

print(w_out)

#############################
# 5. Alternative 2SLS in narrow window
#############################
iv_est <- feols(bond_price ~ 1 | 0 | credit_spread ~ treat,
                data = dat_rdd, cluster = ~issuer_id)
summary(iv_est)

#############################
# 6. Robustness: McCrary density test
#############################
dens_test <- rddensity(dat$running, c = 0)
summary(dens_test)
plot(dens_test)

# Robustness 2: vary bandwidth (½ bw and 2× bw)
for(BW in c(bw/2, bw*2)) {
  cat("=== Bandwidth:", BW, "\n")
  print(rdrobust(y = dat$bond_price[abs(dat$running) <= BW],
                 x = dat$running[abs(dat$running) <= BW],
                 fuzzy = dat$treat[abs(dat$running) <= BW],
                 h = BW))
}
```

-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Theory predicts that slipping from investment- to speculative-grade increases credit spreads by roughly 150 bp. The local Wald estimate should show:  
• Bond price decline of ~1–1.5 % per 100 bp increase in spread (consistent with duration ~5 yrs).  
• Trading volume likely rises (distress trading, index selling) by 10–20 % for a 150 bp jump.

Therefore, I expect a negative causal effect of higher spreads on prices and a positive effect on turnover.

-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
-------------------------------------------------
C1: No precise manipulation of the running variable ………………… 1  
C2: Covariate balance across the cut-off ………………………………………. 1  
C3: Strong first-stage (discontinuity in spreads) …………………………… 1  
C4: Appropriate bandwidth & polynomial choice …………………………… 0.5 (subject to robustness)  
C5: No other simultaneous discrete shocks at cut-off …………………… 0.5  

Total = 4/5. Overall the design appears credible, with remaining concerns addressed via robustness and placebo tests.
